Morgan: Quick heads-up — we have a reproducible p99 artifact in eu-west-1 tied to a specific path: cross-region fallback + KV cache evictions. Minimal summary below, full trace attached in thread.

Morgan: Symptoms: p95 stable (~70ms) but p99 jumps from 310ms -> ~920ms during short bursts. Correlates with requests routed to fallback pool (ap-south-1) due to transient local capacity pressure. Also see KV eviction spikes at the same time.

Morgan: Short profiler excerpt (06:12 trace):
```
req=abc123  route=eu->fallback(ap-south-1)  kernel=quant-q8_0  microbatch=16
kv_lookups=4  kv_misses=3  remote_fetch_ms=240  queuing_ms=90  service_ms=120
flame: runtime::dispatch -> kernel::exec (hot path) -> kv::remote_fetch
```

Javi: @Morgan can you paste the full flamegraph link? also which kernel variant was active on the fallback nodes?

Morgan: Link: https://perf.internal/fg/1798880000/trace-06-12 (private). Fallback nodes were running quant-q8_0 for that model, while eu-local has a q4_0 variant.

Priya: Quick experiment result: lowering microbatch from 16 -> 8 on a canary reduced p99 from ~920ms -> ~600ms (p95 unchanged). Throughput dropped ~12% but unit-cost improved slightly because fewer remote KV roundtrips (less coalesced eviction pressure).

Theo: Interesting — sounds like a cache-eviction amplification. When batches are large we fill KV segments and cause eviction churn; fallback path amplifies latencies because remote fetches add inter-region RTT. Also kernel mismatch matters: q8 kernel has larger tile working set, so combined with bigger microbatches it increases memory pressure and evictions.

Javi: Is the fallback routing policy doing strict capacity-first selection? Maybe it's preferring the q8 variant because of available slots even though it has worse KV footprint.

Morgan: Routing policy = latency-first w/ capacity fallback. In overload it tries local queued pools, then falls back to other regions when local load > 85%. That threshold is where we see the cascade.

Priya: Possible mitigations:
- temporarily reduce microbatch target from 16 -> 8 for EU model group (cheap quick rollback)
- add kernel hint to prefer q4 variant for cross-zone fallbacks (lower memory footprint)
- increase KV cache soft limit on eu nodes to reduce eviction churn
- add routing bias to prefer same-region cold-warm bins (avoid remote fallback if remote KV miss risk is high)

Theo: +1 on kernel hint. Also we should add a perf test: synthetic replay with p95-style load but a small fraction of long sequences to trigger KV warms/evictions. That isolates tail behavior without hitting production.

infra-bot: [alert] incident-created: INC-2026-0457 — elevated p99 in eu-west-1 (auto-detected). Tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre.

Javi: Can someone run a targeted trace with `--trace-kv --kernel-sampling` and attach the raw profile? Want to see hit/miss timeline and kernel switching events.

Morgan: Will run trace and post results in 20m. Plan: 1) deploy microbatch override canary (eu only) 2) add kernel-favor hint on fallback policy 3) run synthetic replay against fallback nodes to reproduce.

Priya: If the canary looks good I'll push the microbatch override to 50% traffic and watch p99. If not, rollback.

Theo: Also schedule a short config change window to increase KV soft limit by +15% on eu pool — cheap experiment and reversible.

Morgan: Thanks. I'll post the full flamegraph and raw trace once the run completes. For immediate triage: set microbatch=8 canary and hold on kernel swaps until we confirm perf delta. :thumbsup:
